page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-224 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on AMD EPYC 7B13 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 224 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 112 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, supporting instruction set extensions such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, while omitting AVX-512 and AMX extensions. System memory is provisioned at 896 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded computational capabilities, placing the instance in the top 10% for multi-core stress-ng tests and overall PassMark CPU scores. High-throughput in-memory operations are confirmed by Redis SET performance exceeding 187 million operations per second and cached memory read bandwidth reaching 12,510 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread metrics such as single-core stress-ng, single-threaded gzip compression, and Geekbench single-core scores show average execution speeds consistent with standard AMD Zen 3 server cores.

The configuration includes zero dedicated GPUs and does not bundle local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for operational persistence. The lack of hardware accelerators and AVX-512 support manifests in sub-optimal large-model LLM text generation rates. However, the high core density and balanced memory allocation deliver strong resource efficiency for massive horizontally scalable workloads, high-volume database caching, compiled code execution, and high-concurrency static web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-224 is a general-purpose instance featuring 224 dedicated vCPUs and 896 GB of system memory powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors on the x86_64 architecture. Designed with a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the system delivers high multi-threaded performance, ranking in the top tier for multi-core stress-ng, PassMark CPU evaluation, and Redis SET throughput reaching over 187 million operations per second. Hardware includes 112 physical cores with symmetric multithreading, hardware encryption via AES and SHA-NI, and standard AVX support, without AVX-512 or bundled local storage. Because local disks and GPUs are absent, the instance depends on remote persistent storage and is unsuited for accelerated deep learning. It remains highly cost-efficient for core-dense parallel execution, distributed caching, software compilation, batch compute pipelines, and large-scale web services requiring extensive thread concurrency and stable memory capacity.
